body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\), heavy arms, fixed folds, and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the learner satisfies, up to a fixed power of \(\log n\), \[\sup_{d_a(x)\ge n^{-b_0}}|\log\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\log\pi_a(x)|=O_P(\delta_{a,n}),\] \[\left|\int m_{a,\tau}(x)\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}dP_X(x)\right|=O_P\left(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}+J_n^{\alpha_a}/n\right),\] and the corresponding relative-error square integral is \(O_P(J_n^{-2s}+J_n^{\alpha_a}/n)\). For \(J_n=\lfloor n^\xi\rfloor\) with \(1/\{s(\alpha_a+1)\}<\xi<1/(\alpha_a+1)\), there exists a deterministic \(M_n\uparrow\infty\) such that the sample-relevant punctured error obeys \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\), and \(\max_{\tau}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|=o_P(1)\). At \(\alpha_a=3/2\), \(s=3/2\), and \(J_n=\lfloor n^{0.3}\rfloor\), the displayed log-error is \(O_P(n^{-1/8}\operatorname{polylog}n)\) and the signed functional is \(O_P(n^{-17/40}\operatorname{polylog}n)\); hence any sufficiently slow \(M_n\) makes the amplified error vanish.
body.justification: This is the early kill test and now derives, rather than assumes, the corrected amplified oracle-transfer condition.
body.gap: Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder control a regular-overlap likelihood projection, not this singular signed Hall-boundary functional.
body.consumer: The lemma supplies a primitive flexible first stage for the non-Gaussian quantile argmin.
